imp.title: fwsign: redundant-compute and stored-signature equality gate for the vendor root key
imp.threat: A single bit flip on the signing host (Rowhammer, bad DRAM, cosmic ray, a glitched appliance) during the one-shot vendor sign yields a signature that still verifies but whose top-layer WOTS key has signed a wrong bottom-tree root. C10 has d=2 and only 512 top-layer leaves (sphincs-c10/src/params.rs:22-31), and fwsign signs deterministically (`None` OptRand), so a later correct re-sign of the same digest (the documented reproducible re-sign workflow) uses the SAME top-layer WOTS key on a different value. Publishing both gives the grafting attacker two WOTS signatures under one key: the precondition for a firmware forgery under the key the WRP-frozen FSBL trusts forever, with no rotation path (#486). The same exposure arises from a faulty signature plus any valid release signature landing in the same top leaf (1 in 512 per pair).
imp.proposal:
1. In `build_signed_manifest`, replace sign-once plus self-verify with the `c10_sign_verified` shape adapted to a host: sign twice with independently reconstructed `SigningKey`s (re-open the blob and re-derive, separate heap buffers, ideally a second process), require byte-equality of the two 4008-byte signatures, then verify, and refuse to emit on any mismatch. The `None` path is deterministic, so equality is exact. Do not copy the MCU glitch furniture (CFI counter, sentinels); the host fault model is memory corruption, so the value is in independent recomputation, not in branch hardening.
2. Make the ledger carry `digest -> sha256(signature)` and read it back before emitting: if the digest was signed before, the new signature must be byte-identical or fwsign hard-fails and prints both hashes. This is compatible with the reproducible re-sign workflow that main.rs:144-148 cites as the reason the ledger is record-only (identical bytes pass); it only removes the silent-divergence case. Keep version monotonicity out of scope (F11 stays as decided).
3. Add a two-machine mode: `fwsign sign --emit-sig-only` on machine A and B, then `fwsign assemble --sig A --sig B` which refuses unless both are byte-equal and verify. Cross-machine equality is the only check that survives a persistent fault on one host (stuck DRAM cell, the correlated-fault residual threat-model.md:603 already names for the device).
4. Add a `fwsign verify-archive` sweep that fails if any two published bundles under one vendor fingerprint carry different signatures for the same digest, and run it in the release checklist.
5. Add host tests with a fault-injection seam (flip one byte of the second signature, or of the stored ledger hash) proving each refusal fires; put them in a path that actually runs.
6. Update threat-model.md §7.9 row :317 so the Genet mitigation column no longer reads as covering all C10 signers; name fwsign explicitly until this lands.

imp.title: Decide vendor-key custody: detached-digest signing with a dedicated pq1 unit as the candidate appliance
imp.threat: The vendor key is a passphrase-encrypted file opened on a general-purpose PC: the secret seed sits in host RAM beside a browser-class attack surface, exposed to malware, Rowhammer and cold-boot, and no HSM implements bespoke SPHINCS+C10. Theft is silent and permanent because the FSBL key cannot rotate after WRP plus RDP-2 (#486). M07's skeptic correction 13 already records that 'colder custody' is undefined until #69 defines any custody.
imp.proposal:
Write the custody decision into #69 as an owner-decision record before any production key is generated, with these options costed:
(a) Air-gapped laptop only (today's doc), plus X2a's two-machine equality. Cheapest; seed still in commodity RAM.
(b) Dedicated pq1 unit as signing appliance: a separate, fenced firmware profile (never a wallet image, never a wallet seed) holding the vendor seed XOR-split across OPTIGA and SE050 behind the SE PIN, with one command that takes a 121-byte manifest preimage (or today's digest), renders version, epoch, slot and both image hashes on the trusted display, requires the chord gesture, and signs through `c10_sign_verified` (double-compute, compare, verify). The appliance must use the deterministic `None` OptRand path so two appliances, or an appliance and an offline host, can be compared byte-for-byte per X2a.
(c) Two appliances in separate custody, both required to produce identical bytes; this gives a 2-person rule without a multi-signature scheme, which SPHINCS+ cannot express (#486 declined cosi).
Independently of the choice, split fwsign now into `digest` (print the preimage hash, no key) and `assemble` (insert an externally produced signature, verify, pack), so the key-holding step is replaceable without touching packaging. Record the appliance's signature count against the #225 per-key cap on-device (page-123-style tally) so the cap is enforced where the key lives, not in a user-writable JSONL file.

imp.title: Secure-MPU execute-never on all secure SRAM (and on secure flash data pages), as a standalone W^X item split out of the deferred intra-S privilege split (#277)
imp.threat: A single fault that corrupts a PC load (glitched POP {pc}/BX LR, a corrupted stacked return address, or a faulted function-pointer/vtable load) redirects secure-privileged execution into attacker-chosen bytes. Secure SRAM1 (0x3000_0000, 192 K) is executable by default on Cortex-M33 and no image programs MPU_S. The companion controls kilobytes of it: every sign handler TOCTOU-snapshots the NS payload into `SIGN_SNAP_BUF`, a `static mut` in .bss at a FIXED link-time address (deterministic from the reproducible build), holding up to 4096 B of inner calldata per tx (batch max is larger). Executing there runs at the same privilege as master_secret, SLOT_CACHE, the SAES key selector and SE unlock, so one PC fault converts to key exfiltration or a sign with no confirm. Rust memory safety (the recorded reason for deferral) does not address this: no memory-safety bug is needed, only one control-flow fault. The existing double-compute/CFI-counter gates protect the signing chain, not arbitrary execution in a sprayed buffer.
imp.proposal:
Add a small `secure/src/hw/mpu.rs` (Reg32-based, no new unsafe category) programmed in main.rs immediately after SAU/GTZC setup and before the first NS-data copy:
1. Region A: all of SRAM1 S-alias 0x3000_0000..0x3002_FFFF, priv RW, XN=1 (covers stack, .data/.bss incl. SIGN_SNAP_BUF and STATE, and all S-stack copies of NS buffers). Confirm first that no RAM-resident code exists (grep found no `ramfunc`/`.data` link_section in secure/, fsbl/, nonsecure/).
2. Region B: secure flash per-device data pages 123-127 (and manifest/boot-state pages), priv RW/RO, XN=1 - these hold partly attacker-influenced bytes and are executable today.
3. Region C (optional, cheap): peripheral space 0x4000_0000-0x5FFF_FFFF XN (architecturally Device memory is already XN, so this is belt-and-braces only).
4. MPU_CTRL = ENABLE | PRIVDEFENA | HFNMIENA. PRIVDEFENA keeps the default map for everything not listed so this is NOT a privilege split and needs no SVC; HFNMIENA keeps XN live inside HardFault/NMI (Trezor sets the equivalent `LL_MPU_CTRL_HARDFAULT_NMI`). Read back RBAR/RLAR/CTRL with `verify_or_halt` like the SAU lock sequence, and add exact-equality const asserts tying region bounds to the linker symbols/`pqsigner-geometry`.
5. Fault routing: leave MEMFAULTENA clear so the IACCVIOL MemManage escalates to the existing HardFault zeroize+reset handler (main.rs:4682), or enable it and add a MemManage handler identical to HardFault. Do not route to the destructive SE wipe (same rationale as rr-1).
6. Compose with the QEMU mps2-an505 build (an505 M33 has MPU_S) so the gate runs in `make e2e`.
Acceptance test (the stated criterion): a test-only gateway command or debugger-driven test that fills SIGN_SNAP_BUF and a stack array with a `bx lr`/marker sled, then forces PC into it (probe-rs write PC on silicon; a deliberate `fn()` transmute under an e2e-only feature on QEMU) and asserts CFSR.IACCVIOL with MMFAR/stacked PC in the buffer and the zeroize+reset path taken; negative control: same test with the MPU write compiled out must execute the sled.    - `"a\x01b"` and `"abc "` are valid UTF-8, so Trezor shows them as text and does not separate the #154 pairs.
   - Trezor has no length row and no whitespace markers.
   - `is_printable_ascii` (`:38-40`) exists but is not used by Ethereum signing.
   - Only the hex fallback is parity; the ASCII+LF gate, markers and Len row go beyond Trezor.

3. **Marker glyph (unflagged for the legacy font).** Any marker drawn from 0x20..0x7E reintroduces a collision, so it must be outside the payload alphabet.
   - The Len row alone does not give injectivity: `"ab\ncd" + 14 spaces + "ef"` and `"ab" + 14 spaces + "cd\nef"` are both 21 bytes and paint identical 16-column rows without an LF marker.
   - The legacy font table spans 0x20..0x7F (`secure/build.rs:414-416`, 96 glyphs), so 0x7F is the one free slot. Its glyph shape must be checked and it must be excluded from text mode (the proposal's 0x20..0x7E rule already does this).
   - One free slot cannot serve as both end-of-line and trailing-space marker: `"ab "` and `"ab\n"` would collide.
   - Simpler: drop the trailing-space marker. Any line or message ending in a space goes to hex mode, or is refused, as `render_const` does at `pqsigner-erc7730/src/display/render/formatters.rs:1629-1640`. Only one LF marker is then needed.
   - The pixel atlas needs the same single glyph, with `atlas_root.rs` regenerated.

4. **Page budget arithmetic is off.**
   - Personal-sign appends `FINGERPRINT_PAGES = 2` into the same `Pages` buffer (`cmd_sign_offchain.rs:967-980`; `pqsigner-erc7730/src/display/mod.rs:39`).
   - Fixed overhead is therefore 7, leaving 24 message pages out of `MAX_PAGES = 31`.
   - Hex is 24 bytes per page (48 hex characters), so the cap is about 568 B after a Len row. The proposal's 576 figure is roughly right, but its "30 + 5" derivation is not.
   - `Pages::with_len(total)` asserts (`eip1271.rs:355-358`). The renderer must become fallible and refuse before allocating; otherwise an LF-heavy payload (700 LFs is about 234 pages) is a secure-world panic.
   - That signature change touches `cmd_sign_offchain.rs`, `offchain_screens.rs:66-91`, and the hard-coded `legacy_pages()` and `CHARS_PER_PAGE` duplicates at `offchain_screens.rs:50,93-98`.
   - The pixel side must also fit `MAX_SCREENS = 48` (`pqsigner-ui-px/src/screen.rs:99`).
   - Legacy banner width is 16 columns; "personal_sign HEX" is 17 characters.

5. **Acceptance gate is infeasible as written.** A Kani 2-safety proof over two symbolic 700-byte payloads through both renderers will not terminate.
   - Restate as: implement a host-side inverse (transcript to payload) and prove or roundtrip `decode(render(m)) == m`.
   - Use Kani at a small bound, proptest or fuzz at the full 700 B, and the #154 pairs as fixed vectors.
   - Existing tests pin the current behaviour and must flip: `secure/src/display_under_test/pure_tests.rs:1480-1505` asserts `?` for 0x1F, 0x7F and 0xC3.

6. **Placement.** Put the classifier and encoder in `aa` or a small new crate, not `pqsigner-erc7730`, to avoid moving the tree-bound provenance hash. `Pages` lives in `pqsigner-erc7730`, so a dependency edge remains either way.

7. **Hex mode is effectively a blind sign.** Label it loudly, like `! BLIND RAW32`, not as a neutral mode. Non-ASCII UTF-8 statements (accented, CJK) become unreadable hex, which is a functional regression against Trezor's Unicode display; say so.

8. **Scope honesty.** This fixes line structure and injectivity only. It is not SIWE (EIP-4361) clear-signing: domain, URI, chain-id and nonce parsing with origin binding stay untracked per `inv_clearsign.json`.

9. **Pixel wrap collision is still unexecuted.** A line-end space being invisible in `emit_message` (`offchain_screens.rs:109-150`) is plausible, because the line keeps the trailing space byte but paints nothing. Confirm with a test before sizing.

10. **Flash.** The 76,949 B `ui-px` overrun is an existing open owner decision, not something this proposal creates. The shipping legacy path has headroom.

11. **Stale line numbers.** The issue and sweep record cite pre-drift lines (`cmd_sign_offchain.rs:202-206`, `usb-protocol-v2.md:258`). The proposal's own line numbers are correct at HEAD.

imp.title: Structured SIWE (EIP-4361) pages with on-device address and chain cross-checks, shown before the raw message
imp.threat: SIWE login phishing and cross-chain session confusion through CMD_SIGN_OFFCHAIN. Today a SIWE message is painted as an undifferentiated 48-chars-per-page stream with every LF shown as '?', so the domain, URI, chain and nonce are not identifiable fields. A hostile companion or phishing site can present a login for attacker.example, or a message whose Chain ID differs from the request chain_id (the chain the replay-safe hash and the 'Chain:' page are bound to), and the user has no structured cue. A message that merely resembles SIWE (contains 'wants you to sign in with your Ethereum account' but is malformed) gets no warning.
imp.proposal:
Add a strict, no-heap EIP-4361 ABNF parser in a pure workspace crate, run on the S-side copy of the personal_sign payload.
(1) If the payload parses exactly, prepend structured pages: 'Sign-in' banner, Domain (with scheme if present), URI, message Chain ID, Nonce, Statement, and expiry/not-before/resources count when present. The full raw message pages from X7a still follow, so the structured view is additive and the existing scroll-to-end consent gate still covers every signed byte.
(2) Device-enforceable checks: the message address must equal the wallet address shown on the 'Signer' page, else refuse; the message Chain ID versus the request chain_id, on mismatch show a loud warning page (or refuse, owner decision).
(3) If the payload contains the SIWE preamble substring but does not parse, show a loud '! Malformed sign-in' page rather than falling back silently (EIP-4361 says wallets SHOULD warn here).
(4) Budget rule: structured pages plus raw pages must fit MAX_PAGES 31; if not, refuse rather than drop either view.
(5) State in the companion guide that the device displays the domain but cannot verify it against the browser origin; the companion remains responsible for the origin check.
Depends on X7a (LF handling and injective raw pages).

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: no SIWE parser or structured display exists, and the gap is real and untracked. But the threat model is overstated, and the cost is understated.

**What I confirmed in code**
- grep for SIWE/4361 in Rust finds only comments (`proto/src/lib.rs:1257-1263`, `secure/src/nsc_batch_offchain_pure_tests.rs:216`).
- The legacy renderer paints 4 context pages, then raw 48-char pages, then a budget page (`secure/src/tx/display/eip1271.rs:331-440`). `sanitise_byte` turns LF into `?` (`eip1271.rs:503-513`).
- The pixel path does the same sanitising and emits only generic `MSG` screens (`secure/src/tx/display/offchain_screens.rs:101-150`).
- The page budget is feasible: 700 B / 48 = 15 raw pages + 5 fixed = 20, leaving 11 of `MAX_PAGES` 31 (`pqsigner-erc7730/src/display/mod.rs:74`).
- No board change, no FSBL impact, no conflict with a recorded owner decision. The no-precedent claim is stated honestly as "beyond".

**Where the proposal is too optimistic**
1. **The two "device-enforceable checks" are largely redundant as security controls.** The signed value is `personal_sign_replay_safe_hash(chain_id, wallet_addr, msg)` (`aa/src/eip1271.rs:183-198`), with `wallet_addr` derived on-device (`secure/src/nsc/cmd_sign_offchain.rs:892-902`). So the signature is already bound to this wallet and the request chain.
   - A message naming another address yields a signature the verifier's `isValidSignature` call on that address rejects.
   - A message whose Chain ID differs from the request `chain_id` fails ERC-1271 on the message chain, unless the verifier checks on the wrong chain.
   - "Cross-chain session confusion" is therefore mostly closed already. These checks are fail-early correctness, not a new barrier against companion lies.
2. **The primary threat is not mitigated by enforcement.** Phishing via attacker.example is the main case, and the device cannot check the origin. The proposal concedes this. The benefit is only an attentive-user cue.
3. **Cost is understated.** There are two display stacks to implement:
   - the legacy 16x4 pages, with the `context_page_exact` occurrence==1 uniqueness checks (`eip1271.rs:300-322`);
   - the `ui-px` native screens, with paired-constant and trailer-proof discipline, plus Kani census re-lock, fuzz target, and companion docs.
   - A domain or URI can each exceed 48 chars, so structured fields need multi-page wrap rules. "About 4 structured pages" is optimistic.
4. **Flash.** The ship-shaped image has 34,071 B of headroom without `ui-px` and is 76,949 B over with it (CLAUDE.md). A strict ABNF parser (RFC 3986 authority/URI, RFC 3339 dates, EIP-55 keccak check) plus two renderers is plausibly 3-6 KB and is unmeasured. It competes with the open flash-lever decision.
5. **New spoof surface.** A non-SIWE message could lay out raw pages that mimic the structured "Sign-in / Domain:" pages. Raw pages are distinguished only by the `Msg N/M` footer, so structured pages need a distinguishing mark the message cannot paint, plus a uniqueness check like the existing context-page one.
6. **Demand is prospective.** SIWE/WalletConnect is a companion roadmap item (`docs/feature-roadmap-research-2026-06.md:48,59`), not a shipped flow.

**Tracking**
The dependency X7a is the open issue #154 (personal_sign non-injective rendering). No SIWE issue exists. I did not find SIWE among the consolidated master items.

The advisor was rate-limited, so this verdict has no second review.

1. Reframe the threat. Drop "cross-chain session confusion" as a security claim: `replaySafeHash` already binds `chainId` and `address(this)` (`aa/src/eip1271.rs:183-198`). Describe the address and chain checks as fail-early consistency checks plus a user cue. The real value is field legibility (Domain, URI, Nonce, Expiry) and the EIP-4361 SHOULD-warn on malformed look-alikes.
2. Address mismatch should refuse, since the signature is useless anyway. Decide the EIP-55 policy: accept only the exact checksummed form, per ABNF.
3. Chain mismatch should default to warn. A refuse would break dapps that hardcode Chain ID 1, and the resulting signature would not verify on the message chain anyway. Leave refuse as an owner option.
4. Add anti-spoof framing. Structured pages need a marker or footer that raw message pages cannot reproduce, and the existing `context_page_exact` uniqueness check (`eip1271.rs:300-322`) should extend to them.
5. Scope both renderers explicitly: legacy `eip1271.rs` and `ui-px` `offchain_screens.rs`, including paired constants and trailer/Kani proofs. Specify wrap rules for long domain and URI. Refuse on page-budget overflow, as proposed.
6. Add a flash gate: measure with `make size-report-px` before adoption. Do not land while the secure slot is over budget, or put it behind a feature flag until the flash lever is decided.

8. Check whether batch off-chain signing carries PERSONAL_SIGN (I did not confirm this). If it does, apply the same rules or refuse SIWE in a batch.
9. The companion doc must say the device does not verify origin, and nothing may market this as phishing protection.
10. Cost is M-L rather than M, and priority is P3: no enforcement gain over the existing hash binding, no shipped SIWE flow yet, and flash over budget.

imp.title: State the R-incarnation few-time caveat beside P14 and correct the three claim sites that say the slot cap is a true per-key cap
imp.threat: Claim-vs-code gap, not an emergency. A same-seed restore or a second live device starts the slot's device-side tallies at zero for a slot key the previous incarnation already used. Each incarnation caps `userop_sigs + effective_offchain` at 65,536 on its own. imp.title: Bind the page-123 journal key to a public wallet tag and set an explicit keep-on-wipe, erase-on-decommission policy
imp.threat:
Second-hand or re-provisioned device correctness. The page-123 key is `sha256(account, chain, slot)[..8]` with no wallet binding, and no wipe path erases the page. A device wiped and set up with a different seed inherits the previous wallet's registered flags and counts. Three consequences follow:

- The invariant-#9 rule 'post-restore, `CMD_SIGN_OFFCHAIN` for an unregistered slot is rejected' is silently satisfied for the new seed.
- The new wallet's per-slot budgets arrive pre-burned (denial of service only; over-counting is few-time-safe).
- The device-lifetime budget of 128 distinct slots is shared across every seed the device ever holds, so a used device can arrive with new-slot creation already refused.
imp.proposal:
1. **Wallet tag in the key.** Change `slot_key_compute` to hash a non-secret wallet tag first, e.g. `sha256("pq-p123-v2" || wallet_tag || account || chain || slot)[..8]`. Derive `wallet_tag` from public bootstrap material such as the account-0 CREATE2 salt `sha256(masterPkSeed || masterPkRoot)`, or a hash of `masterPkSeed`. Every page-123 consumer already runs after PIN unlock. Whether the master keygen result is cached at each call site (e.g. `CMD_OFFCHAIN_SYNC`, `CMD_OFFCHAIN_STATUS`) is something the implementer must check; I did not trace it.
2. **Keep page 123 on lockout and duress wipe.** Erasing would under-count a same-seed restore on the same device. With the tag, a same-seed restore finds its own counters again and a different seed sees no registrations.
3. **Erase only on an owner-confirmed decommission or RMA path.** Tie it to the sanitisation receipt in #634. This is the only way to hand the 128-slot budget back to a new owner.

imp.title: Make FSBL C10 verifier correctness a freeze gate: replay the 246-vector mutant corpus through the Rust verify path the FSBL links, with executed-count assertion, an FSBL-configured (hw-sha256) leg, and a written proof-scope statement
imp.threat: After WRP + RDP-2 the FSBL's C10 verifier can never be patched. C10 is a bespoke parameter set and tweakable-hash/ADRS encoding with no applicable official KATs and one active user. A wrong-accept bug in the linked verifier (or in its HASH-peripheral SHA-256 backend) is a permanent firmware-forgery primitive on every shipped die; a wrong-reject bug bricks updates. M05 covers faults and M07 covers key policy; neither gates on functional correctness of the frozen verifier.
imp.proposal:
Add one freeze gate, recorded in the M07 package, that must be green on the exact commit whose FSBL is frozen (and before the #541 measurement profile is frozen, so no later verifier edit moves the measured link).

1. Rust leg (the missing one). New host test in fw-manifest (or sphincs-c10) that loads contracts/smart-wallet/test/c10_mutant_corpus.json and contracts/smart-wallet/test/c10_test_vectors.json and runs every entry through sphincs_c10::verify, i.e. the function ManifestRef::verify_signature calls. Assert verdict == expectValid per entry, and assert the executed count equals the committed count (246 = 242 reject + 4 accept today) so an empty or truncated file cannot pass. The corpus verdicts are already bytecode ground truth (forge) and replayed by the Lean spec, so this closes the three-way differential Rust / Yul / Lean on malformed and boundary signatures (count fields, the [3992,4008) straddling tail, ADRS fields).

2. Python-oracle negative leg. independent_c10_signer.py has a verify() (line 259); have it replay the same corpus so the clean-room implementation also agrees on rejects, not only on accepts.

3. FSBL-configuration leg. The frozen binary runs sphincs-c10 with hw-sha256 (STM32 HASH peripheral), which no host test and no QEMU machine exercises. Either run the corpus once on pq1 silicon through an FSBL-configured build (bench harness reporting accept/reject per vector via the existing stage-marker channel, never shipped), or write an explicit out-of-scope line plus the compensating evidence (HASH KAT at boot, positive slot-A verify on silicon). Decide which at the review; do not leave it implicit.

4. Enrol the feature-gated C10 tests that run in no CI suite (#722: primitive_kat, near_miss_validate, fors_*), since the per-primitive KAT is the localisation tool if leg 1 ever disagrees.

5. Proof-scope statement, written into the freeze record: what is machine-checked (piecewise Aeneas extractions: ADRS, auth-path loop, WOTS pk-from-sig, tweakable hash, FORS index, WOTS digits), what is corpus-tier only (whole hypertree::verify composition in Rust; no end-to-end extraction target exists), what is assumed (HASH peripheral == FIPS 180-4, compiler). Note that the signature is a fixed [u8; 4008], so length malformation is not expressible at this layer and belongs to the fw-manifest structural tests.

No new code enters the FSBL; cost is tests plus one optional bench run.

No FSBL bytes, no board change, no conflict with a recorded decision (it is the "audit the single verifier" alternative to the declined hybrid). Not implemented; #304 is the nearest tracker and does not name the corpus or the freeze.

But the proposal overstates what the corpus buys, and mis-ranks its own legs:

1. The corpus cannot detect the bug class that matters most for a frozen +C verifier. All 242 rejects are mutations of ONE signature (valid-1) under ONE key: 204 generic byte/bit flips, 16 tail flips, 8 zero-regions, 8 count flips, 3 degenerate, 3 perturbations. Every one breaks a hash chain or H_msg, so a Rust verifier with the forced-zero gate (sphincs-c10/src/hypertree.rs:380-382) or the WOTS target-sum gate (sphincs-c10/src/wots.rs:178) deleted still agrees with the corpus on all 246. Those gates are exactly what makes C10 non-standard and forgeable if absent. The test that does cover them is sphincs-c10/tests/near_miss_validate.rs (secret-key-built near-miss, rejected only by the targeted gate), which sits behind `near-miss-gen` and runs in no CI suite (#722). So leg 4, presented as a "localisation tool", is the load-bearing leg; leg 1 is the cheap complement.

2. "Rust negatives are not a differential" is wrong for the KAT file. c10_test_vectors.json verdicts are Rust-judged and then asserted by forge on bytecode and by Lean, so Rust/Yul/Lean already agree on those 10 vectors (6 rejects). The real gap is narrower: the 236 extra mutant points, plus the gate-specific near-misses not being run.

3. The straddling-tail [3992,4008) class is a Yul calldataload artefact (gen_mutant_corpus.py docstring); against a fixed Rust array it is just 16 more byte flips. Do not credit it as Rust boundary coverage.

4. The hw-sha256 threat is overstated. FSBL and secure world share one driver (fsbl/src/hash.rs:66 calls pqsigner_hw::hash::init_clock; secure/src/hw/hash.rs:1-14 re-exports the same crate). That driver has produced signatures on pq1 silicon that verified offline, and the FSBL positively verifies slot A on silicon. A HASH-backend defect yields wrong-reject, since accept needs a 16-byte root equality against the pinned vendor root; wrong-accept by a backend bug is not a credible path. Caveat: the boot KAT is single-block "abc" only, so multi-block/merge-buffer conformance rests on those positive verifies, which the scope line must say. The silicon corpus run should be dropped in favour of the scope line, removing the bench-harness risk.

5. False-precedent nuance. Trezor's Ed25519 hedge targets a flaw in the scheme; a three-implementation differential shares one spec and cannot see a scheme or parameter flaw (independent_signer_xcheck.rs:14-15 says "not a second spec"). The gate is not a substitute for the declined hybrid and the freeze record must say so. Related: Lean and Yul verdicts on the corpus come from a Python Yul replica validated on only 10 vectors then confirmed by forge, so ground truth is bytecode, fine.

6. Count assertion: the forge leg only requires `entries.length >= 240` (SPHINCsC10AsmMutantCorpus.t.sol:58) and the Lean leg prints totals. Pin the exact count and reject-count in all legs, not only the new Rust one.

Leg 1 placed in default-feature sphincs-c10 tests is picked up by CI (ci.yml:230); the feature-gated tests are not, which is the #722 failure mode recurring. Also the verify source is frozen only if the FSBL build's sphincs-c10 tree hash is recorded alongside the green run.

The critic's premise that a firmware decision gates this does not hold: the on-chain route already works, so no firmware change is needed.

Both are CMD_SIGN_USEROP, which commits last_userop_count at sign time, so MAX_OFFCHAIN_GAP never applies. - Covered only when pq1's approval is required in every quorum (n-of-n, or all owners are pq1). If classical owners alone can reach threshold, both the PQ property and the on-device-decode property are lost.

imp.proposal:

imp.title: Masked blind binary restore: enter the 24 words as 264 button bits under a per-bit on-screen one-time mapping, with no echo, so neither the display bus nor the button nets alone carry a seed bit
imp.threat: A passive logic-level tap on the NV3007 SPI bus (the one implant class confirmed in the wild: seed read off the SE-to-display bus, exfiltrated over LTE). Today every seed-bearing wizard screen puts seed glyphs on MOSI in the clear: show_mnemonic on create, typed letters and the candidate list on restore, and the 3-word quiz on create. M03 states that no firmware encoding hides MOSI from a logic-level tap; M10 is a P3 study; M11 is an MP board respin. NOT in scope: an implant that taps the display bus AND both button nets (it recovers everything), malicious firmware, or a camera on the user's paper.
imp.proposal:
Add a third wizard option beside 'New Wallet' and 'Restore' (seed_wizard.rs choose_setup_mode), restore-only, opt-in.

1. Entry. The user enters 24 x 11 = 264 bits (the standard BIP-39 indices including the 8-bit checksum), one bit per Short press. Before each bit the device draws a fresh mask bit r_i and shows only the mapping, e.g. 'LEFT = 1' or 'RIGHT = 1', plus a public position counter ('word 7 bit 4'). The secret bit is s_i = press_i XOR r_i. Nothing derived from s_i is ever rendered: no echo, no word, no candidate list. The repaint after a press must be identical for either button.

2. Why the mask and not plain coin-flip entry. Plain blind entry (L=0, R=1) keeps the display bus clean but puts the seed in the clear on PA0/PA1, which are slower and easier to tap than SPI. With the mask, the display bus sees r (uniform, independent of the seed) and the button nets see s XOR r (uniform); each channel alone reveals no bit. This is the same shape as invariant #1's dual-SE XOR split, applied to the two human-interface channels. It generalises F-20 (random PIN start digit, pin_entry.rs:10-23) from 'hide the start' to a full one-time pad.

3. Button model. Count only (Left,Short) and (Right,Short). (Left,Long) = undo one bit (redraw a fresh r_i). Ignore (Right,Long) and the 80 ms chord until all 264 bits are in, otherwise thumb skew ends entry early (buttons.rs:183-189). Call timeout::reset_activity on every event as the other dialogs do.

4. Mask source. One rng_strong::fill of 33 bytes per attempt, zeroized with the bit buffer. Do not use rng::byte_nonsecret: r is secret-equivalent once combined with a button tap.

5. Validation and confirmation. Pack to indices and call the existing Mnemonic::from_indices (bip39/src/full.rs:200); a bad checksum shows the existing public 'Bad checksum' status. A typo passes the checksum with probability 1/256, so the user then confirms the public wallet address with the existing show-on-device path (CMD_GET_WALLET_ADDRESS arg2=1, cmd_get_wallet_address.rs:26-33) after setup. No new derivation code.

6. User-side material. Publish a printable BIP-39 word -> 11-bit table and a one-page procedure so the conversion is done by hand, never on a computer. Document that an offline-generated seed (dice or coin) restored this way is a wallet whose seed never crossed the display bus; this is the zero-RNG-change answer the M18 skeptic pointed at.

7. Testability. Put the bit packing, mask application and undo logic in a workspace crate (bip39 or pqsigner-domain) with host tests and a differential test against from_indices. secure/src/ui is excluded from host tests, so tests written there never run.

8. Docs. Replace the 'targeted hardware implants remain the residual' sentence in user-device-verification.md:163-168 with the scoped claim: display-only tap defeated on this path, dual display+button tap not. Add the row to the threat model next to M03 channel 3.

Keeps: the existing letter-based Restore unchanged as the default; rng_strong::fill(&mut entropy) on NewWallet untouched, so scripts/rng_consumer_audit.py REQUIRED_THREE_SOURCE stays green. Fits the #250 'Check backup' constraint (entry-based, never display-based) and can serve as its entry path later.

All sit on one package edge, a few millimetres apart. An implant that taps the display at the MCU gets both button nets with two more low-speed wires. The firmware is open, so an implant built for pq1 will take them. The item only defeats an implant that taps at the panel connector and was not adapted to pq1. I did not trace the button routing in the schematic or PCB layers; if the buttons share the display flex, the core fails.

2. **The offline dice/coin seed claim (step 6) is broken.** A hand-generated 256-bit seed has no valid 24th word until SHA-256 is computed, and from_indices rejects a bad checksum (bip39/src/full.rs:200-206). The user must either use a computer, or the device must accept 256 bits with no typo detection. The step-5 address check does not help either: a fresh seed has no known-good address to compare against.

With "LEFT = 1" shown, entering a 0 needs an extra inference step, and the two hands differ in speed. Latency therefore correlates with s or with the press, and the "display alone reveals nothing" claim holds only for the algebra.

4. **Usability is worse than risk 2 states.** At a 1% slip rate, 264 blind presses succeed about 7% of the time, and a failure cannot be located.

X1a would have stopped that implant as built. Trezor matrix recovery splits the secret between a trusted device screen and an untrusted host; here both channels sit on the same untrusted board, so it is an analogy, not parity.

imp.title: Make USB-01's optional BASEPRI_S mask mandatory across every verify-paint-proof bracket, fix the sau.rs PRIS comment, and prove it with a hostile NS SysTick on silicon
imp.threat: Same swap-and-restore as X5a, limited to the CPU path: a hostile NS arms the banked NS SysTick (or pends NS PendSV) before calling a sign veneer, and its handler runs on top of the secure thread parked in the pixel dialog. From there it can reprogram a glyph page between the two atlas hashes, or re-enter the gateway (USB-01). USB-01's compare-and-swap try-enter refuses the re-entry but does not stop the NS handler running or writing flash.
imp.proposal:
1. Add an RAII guard that sets BASEPRI_S = 0x80 and restores the previous value on drop. Hold it from before verify_atlas until after atlas_root_proof in px_confirm and px_confirm_plain, and around the unbracketed paints (screens::show_with, paint_legacy, film_start_with through film_resolve).
2. Preferably take it once at every cmse-nonsecure-entry veneer together with USB-01's try-enter, so one mechanism serves both items.
3. Confirm from the ARMv8-M ARM (DDI 0553) that with AIRCR.PRIS=1 all NS configurable exceptions sit at 0x80 or lower priority and are masked by BASEPRI_S=0x80. I could not fetch the ARM page; treat the semantics as unverified until checked.
4. Check what else the mask stops. Secure SysTick is at 0x00 and keeps running (button sampling, idle timer, IWDG kick). Secure PendSV is at 0xFF and is deferred for the bracket; decide whether the idle re-unlock may be deferred that long. I found no NVIC priority writes in main.rs or hw/, so secure IRQs (TZIC, TAMP) appear to stay at 0, but that needs a direct check.
5. Rewrite the comment at sau.rs:709-716: PRIS only ranks secure handlers above NS ones; it does not stop an NS exception preempting secure thread mode.
6. Source-invariant test: every caller of verify_atlas / atlas_verified holds the guard. Put it in a workspace crate or a *_pure_tests file, since secure/src/ui and nsc are cfg(not(test)).
7. Silicon test, no visual check (the pq1 bench has no LCD): an NS fixture arms SysTick_NS at 1 kHz, bumps a counter in NS RAM and attempts a nested veneer call. Pass = the counter does not advance between dialog entry and exit, read out afterwards. QEMU cannot show this; its gateway is a mailbox.
imp.rationale: The USB-01 feasibility review lists BASEPRI_S=0x80 only as an optional addition to the try-enter. For the atlas bracket it is the cheap layer that removes the simplest attack, and it also backs the 'non-reentrant dispatcher' SAFETY comments. It is not sufficient alone: it does nothing against an NS DMA write or a fault on the flash read, which is why X5a is the primary fix. If USB-01 lands with the veneer-level mask, this item reduces to the comment fix, the source test and the silicon fixture.

skeptic.reason:
Not refuted. The core holds, but the scope, the risk list and the silicon test need correcting.

**What I confirmed in code**
- No BASEPRI/PRIMASK/FAULTMASK use anywhere in secure/src, nonsecure/src or fsbl/src (grep, zero hits).
- AIRCR.PRIS is set with BFHFNMINS=0 (secure/src/sau.rs:648,702), and the comment at sau.rs:712-716 does say PRIS=0 is what lets "an NS IRQ preempt a secure veneer mid-handler". That is wrong.
- The verify-paint-proof bracket is unmasked: verify_atlas at secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1090 and :1126, atlas_root_proof at :1104 and :1146.
- Secure SysTick is at 0x00 and secure PendSV at 0xFF (secure/src/main.rs:885-888).
- No ITNS write exists and nonsecure/src has no exception handlers, so the only preempting vectors are the banked NS system exceptions. A benign NS image loses nothing from the mask.
- Not implemented and not tracked: my issue search found no BASEPRI or NS-exception-masking issue.

**What I did not verify**
- The BASEPRI_S=0x80 / PRIS=1 semantics. I did not fetch ARM DDI 0553 either. From memory of the architecture, PRIS=1 maps NS priorities into 0x80-0xFF and BASEPRI_S=0x80 masks that whole range; I am fairly confident, but step 3 of the proposal stays a hard precondition.
- Whether TZIC and TAMP sit at priority 0. I found no NVIC priority (IPR) write in secure/src, which suggests they do; I did not open tzic.rs:138 or tamp.rs:344 to confirm.

**Budget, decisions, precedent**
- Flash cost is a few instructions; the FSBL is untouched; no board change.
- No conflict with a recorded owner decision.
- Trezor sets PRIS (core/embed/sec/trustzone/stm32u5/tz_init.c:136) but its only BASEPRI use is SEGGER RTT locking, so "no direct precedent" is accurate. The TF-M mention is unfetched and should not carry weight.

**Residual (the proposal already admits most of it)**
- It does nothing against NS DMA or a fault on the flash read; X5a remains the primary fix.
- A pended NS exception fires the moment the guard drops. That gives NS only a refusal (the sign handler re-proves the atlas before release, e.g. secure/src/nsc/cmd_sign_userop.rs:1944), not a swap-and-restore.
skeptic.corrections:
1. **Step 2 (veneer-level guard) is not sufficient alone; the PendSV re-unlock dialog is outside any veneer.**
   - The idle re-unlock runs PIN entry from secure PendSV at priority 0xFF (secure/src/main.rs:4490).
   - With PRIS=1, NS SysTick maps to about 0x80, which outranks 0xFF and preempts that handler.
   - The PIN screen paints through the atlas: secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:183-184 calls px::screens::show, which calls verify_atlas (secure/src/ui/px/screens.rs:111).
   - Fix: the guard must sit at the atlas call sites (step 1), or the PendSV handler must take it too. The source-invariant test must cover screens.rs:111/142/167, lcd.rs:422/526/574/627 and the PendSV path, not just the veneers.
   - Boot and seed-wizard paints (seed_wizard.rs:75) run before NS starts and are not exposed.

2. **The PendSV-deferral risk (step 4 and the risks field) is moot for guarded handlers.**
   - The only PENDSVSET writer is main.rs:4361, gated by `!nsc::handler_is_busy()` at :4350.
   - A parked sign dialog therefore never pends secure PendSV, and the mask defers nothing new.
   - It matters only for the five handlers without HandlerGuard (#152), which are short.

3. **The "starves the NS USB IRQ" objection in imp/USB-01 does not apply.** No interrupt is retargeted to NS and NS polls, so a whole-veneer BASEPRI_S mask costs a benign NS nothing. That makes the veneer-level placement cheap, as a complement to correction 1, not a replacement.

4. **The silicon test (step 7) is vacuous as written.**
   - `e2e-test` short-circuits the pixel confirm (secure/src/ui/px/confirm_px.rs:90-109), so the dialog window is near zero.
   - The pq1 bench has no LCD, and trusted-UI flows have never run on pq1 silicon (#700).
   - It needs a negative control: build once with the guard compiled out and show the NS counter does advance.
   - The secure side must snapshot the NS-RAM counter at bracket entry and exit. NS can only see the whole veneer, and one pended tick always fires after unmask, so an NS-side "did not advance" check is off by one.
   - It needs a fixture that holds the bracket open for a known time without buttons or a panel.

5. **Restore, never clear.** If BASEPRI_S is left at 0x80 on return to NS, every NS exception stays masked. The guard must restore the saved value on every exit path, including early `?` returns. As an RAII guard it will, but the test should assert BASEPRI_S is 0 at veneer return.

6. **Pin secure IRQ priorities with a test.** Add a source test that no secure IRQ is ever given a priority of 0x80 or lower, since the guard would silently mask it.

7. **Step 3 stays a hard precondition.** The PRIS/BASEPRI_S semantics are unverified by both the proposer and me. Check DDI 0553 and observe it on silicon through the negative control before the comment rewrite claims anything.

8. **Comment fixes.** Besides sau.rs:709-716, fix the "non-reentrant dispatcher" SAFETY claims listed in verify/USB-01 (nsc/mod.rs:1001-1003, 1024, 1915; cmd_sign_offchain.rs:131).

9. **Cost and placement.** Cost is M, not S, because of the fixture and the PendSV path. Keep P2. This is best landed as a sub-item of USB-01, and it must not be presented as closing the atlas swap without X5a.
